summary.title: Creating Rust/C++ polyglot Fibonacci main.rs
summary.body:
I wrote the polyglot to `polyglot/main.rs`. It compiles with both `rustc` and `g++ -x c++` with no warnings, and both programs print the same results: f(0)=1, f(1)=1, f(2)=2, f(3)=3, f(10)=89, f(50)=20365011074, f(90)=4660046610375530309.

**How it works:**
- **First line `/*/* */`:** C++ block comments don't nest, so for C++ this is a complete comment and it goes on to compile the C++ code below it. Rust comments do nest, so Rust is still inside a comment and skips the C++ code.
- **`#if 0` then `// */`:** C++ stops compiling from `#if 0` onward and reads `// */` as a line comment. Rust only looks for `*/` inside a block comment, so this line ends its comment and Rust compiles the Rust code that follows.
- **End of file (`// \`, `/*`, `#endif`, `// */`):** In C++, the backslash at the end of `// \` joins the next line into the comment, so the `/*` is ignored and C++ sees the `#endif`. Rust treats `// \` as an ordinary line comment, then `/*` opens a comment that hides `#endif`, and `// */` closes it.

**Limits:**
- Both versions use 64-bit unsigned integers, so the answer is only correct up to N=92. Above that, the numbers wrap around in both languages; the Rust version uses `wrapping_add` so it doesn't panic.
- `rustc /path/main.rs` writes the `main` binary to the directory you run it from, not next to the source file. Your command `.../polyglot/main N` therefore only works if you run `rustc` from inside `polyglot/`, or add `-o /tmp/obench-cell-53plv864/bench_opencode_polyglot-rust-c_n_soo_db/polyglot/main`.
